subject: Caching impact on pricing — follow-up & numbers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Turner <ethan.turner@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Caching impact on pricing — follow-up & numbers

Hi Ethan — great to speak earlier. Quick recap + a few asks so we can build a tight pricing/MAF for your pilot: 

Recap:
- Use case: conversational product support + a small batch rerank for search results.
- Pilot horizon: 3 months (pilot) with goal to scale to full roll-out in ~6 months.
- Key unknowns we need to confirm to size and price accurately: expected monthly token volumes (pilot vs scale), target budget range, and what you expect for repeated/prefix reuse (which drives cache hit).

As discussed, attached is the post-call deck and the pricing calc (live sheet link below). To unblock pricing we specifically need:
1) A realistic monthly token range (pilot and anticipated scale).
2) Target effective price you want to land at (e.g. $/1M tokens effective after caching).
3) Any enterprise constraints (SLA, dedicated capacity interest).

High-level caching assumptions I used in the sample calc (attached):
- List unit price used for examples: $150 / 1M tokens (this is our baseline list for the model family we discussed).
- Prefix cache semantics: KV cache for repeated prefixes/context — tokens served from cache are not billed.
- Example hit-rate buckets we typically see: low (10-25%), mid (25-45%), high (45-65%) — depends on prompt standardization and session repeat patterns.

Why this matters: effective $/1M = list_price * (1 - hit_rate). So you can see small changes in hit rate materially move monthly spend. I put 25/40/60% buckets in the sheet so you can see monthly cost at each volume.

Next steps: if you can reply with the two numbers above (pilot tokens / scaled tokens and target budget), I’ll send a short pricing proposal and recommended pilot telemetry to validate cache hit on your traffic.

Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FASTRETAIL-pricing-calc
Attachments: postcall-deck.pdf, pricing-calc-FASTRETAIL.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Caching impact on pricing — follow-up & numbers

Thanks Marissa — appreciated the recap and the sheet. A few numbers from our side to plug in: 

Current (pilot) estimate: 10-20M tokens / month (we expect higher per-session repetition during pilot because of a limited user set).
Target scale (6 months): 80-120M tokens / month as we roll across more regions/features.
Budget: pilot budget in the $5k-8k / month range; if we hit target scale we could commit $15k-25k / month depending on unit economics.
Target effective $/1M: our finance / procurement are looking for effective ~$90-120 per 1M tokens after caching to be greenlit at scale.

Couple of asks: can you show the effective monthly cost for 80M & 120M tokens at 25%, 40%, and 60% hit rates (we want to understand the sensitivity)? Also, does Redwood bill for prefix tokens used from cache (we assume not) and are there any minimums for a pilot?

Ethan Turner
Product Lead — AI Experiences
FastRetail

Marissa — quick internal note before you respond to Ethan: 
- Good ask on the hit-rate buckets. For commercials, we typically show three scenarios (conservative/mid/aggressive) using list_price = $150 / 1M as your deck does.
- Confirm billing: cache-served tokens are not billed (we should note this in the proposal and reference the telemetry we'll provide).
- Pilot offer: suggest we propose a capped pilot not-to-exceed (e.g., $8k/mo) for the first 2 months with telemetry and a 30% nominal discount on list for committed volume if they sign a 12-month reserved capacity at scale. That gives them runway to measure hit-rate.
- Also add a note: hit-rates vary by product — chat with product about expected system prompt repetition: for templated chat flows 40-50% is realistic; for open-ended user queries expect 10-30%.

If you want, I can pre-fill a second tab in the sheet with the reserved-commit discount slicer.

- Marcus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Caching impact on pricing — follow-up & numbers

Thanks Ethan — see the quick sensitivity calc below (I also updated the Google sheet/tab):

Assumptions: list_price = $150 per 1M tokens; cache-served tokens not billed; effective $/1M = list_price * (1 - hit_rate).

Buckets (effective $/1M):
- 25% hit: $150 * (1 - 0.25) = $112.50 / 1M
- 40% hit: $150 * (1 - 0.40) = $90.00 / 1M
- 60% hit: $150 * (1 - 0.60) = $60.00 / 1M

Monthly cost examples (scaled volumes):
- 80M tokens/month:
  - 25% hit -> $112.50 * 80 = $9,000 / month
  - 40% hit -> $90.00 * 80 = $7,200 / month
  - 60% hit -> $60.00 * 80 = $4,800 / month

- 120M tokens/month:
  - 25% hit -> $112.50 * 120 = $13,500 / month
  - 40% hit -> $90.00 * 120 = $10,800 / month
  - 60% hit -> $60.00 * 120 = $7,200 / month

Interpretation vs your target: you indicated finance is targeting $90-120 per 1M effective. That maps to roughly the 25-40% hit buckets at these list prices — e.g., at 40% hit you land at $90/1M which yields ~$7.2k / month at 80M tokens (within your pilot-to-scale budgets).

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Pilot telemetry: we’ll run a 2-week sampling to measure real prefix reuse and report an empirical hit rate (we'll provide a small instrumentation guide).
2) Pilot commercial: propose a capped pilot (NTE $8k/month) for 2 months to gather telemetry and validate hit.
3) If telemetry supports >=40% hit at scale, we can move to a reserved capacity quote with a 30% commit discount (Marcus will draft).

I’ll send a short proposal doc + pilot SOW once you confirm you’re comfortable with the pilot cap and sampling plan.

Attachments: pricing-calc-FASTRETAIL.xlsx (updated)
Link: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FASTRETAIL-pricing-calc
